# bugs #2672: mcs51: peephole rule 107 removes the last two entries of an ljmp jump table

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2672/
- Category: [Analyzed, not fixed](../../unresolved.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Keep open. Peephole rule 107 of mcs51 needs a condition that excludes jump tables.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17176 the file `sp_sfc_operation_handler.c` of the attached project gets wrong code with the
ticket's options `--model-large --opt-code-speed`. The float expression and `expf` are not
involved. The `switch` on `sfc_state` in `error_check` has case values 0 to 8, and its jump table
has entries for 0 to 6 only. For the value 8, `SFC_INV_RUNNING_OVL`, the jump arrives three bytes
after the start of the first block of the switch body. The code in comment 9 sets that state, and
the next call of the function fails.

A harness that includes the file called `sfc_operation_handler` twice in ucsim. The second call
has the state 8 and inputs for which `ERROR_INV_OVL` is correct. In the large model with
`--opt-code-speed`, the call skips the two instructions that compute the address of `dig4`, tests a
bit of another byte, and reports `ERROR_INV_DC_OFFSET`. In the medium model with
`--opt-code-speed`, the call does not return and `main` starts again and again. Both models give
`ERROR_INV_OVL` without `--opt-code-speed` and with `--no-peep`.

The function below shows the defect without `--opt-code-speed`. It was run in the small, medium,
and large models and with `--stack-auto`. `f (4)` returns 0xa3 and does not set `g`. With
`--no-peep` it sets `g`.

```c
unsigned char g;

unsigned char f (unsigned char s)
{
  switch (s)
    {
    case 4:
    case 3:
      g = 0x33;
      return 0xa3;
    case 0:
      return 0xa0;
    case 1:
      return 0xa1;
    case 2:
      return 0xa2;
    }
  return 0xff;
}
```

## Known

`genJumpTab` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` emits a table of `ljmp` instructions for a switch with at most 7
table entries, and with at most 16 under `--opt-code-speed`. Larger tables hold addresses in `.db`
lines. The switch of the ticket has 9 entries, so it gets the `ljmp` table only with the option.

When the block of the highest case values is the first block of the switch body, the last entries
of the table are `ljmp` instructions to the label that follows the table. Peephole rule 107 in
`src/mcs51/peeph.def` replaces `ljmp %1` before `%1:` with the label, and its only condition is
`labelRefCountChange(%1 -1)`. It removes the last entry and then each entry before it that has the
same target. With `--fverbose-asm` the comment of rule 107 appears twice at the end of the table.
After one removal the code is still correct, because the index of that entry selects the address
that follows the table. After two removals the highest index selects an address three bytes
further.

The comment in `genJumpTab` states that peephole rules must not change the table. `src/SDCCpeeph.c`
has the condition `notInJumpTable` for that purpose, and rule 107 does not use it.

## Open

Rule 107 needs a condition that keeps it away from the entries of a jump table, or that limits it
to the last entry. `notInJumpTable()` costs three bytes in each table whose last entry rule 107
removes today. Neither was tried. The other rules that match `ljmp` were not checked for the same
defect. The revision after which the reporter's build failed in October 2017 was not identified.

## Related

Bug #4066, fixed in [r16836](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/16836/), was damage of the same
kind by the rule that replaces `sjmp %5` with `ljmp %6`. That rule was 257.b before r16836 and is
257.c on r17176. The fix added `notInJumpTable()` to it.
